result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers place all eight pieces with clear sizes, distance tiers and no interaction, so either layout could be drawn. B gives alarms the largest central block with the turbine grid directly beneath, and adds useful operator details: curtailment relabels the output gap, planned maintenance gets its own neutral tile state, and the alarm-threshold advice keeps red rare. A's reading order is a little cleaner, with the least urgent items at the bottom of the screen, but B is slightly stronger overall. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers place all eight pieces with drawable diagrams, distance tiers and sensible grouping, so they are close. A puts the alarm list in the largest block, directly above the turbine grid. It also adds useful details: label a curtailed gap as curtailment rather than a shortfall, give planned maintenance its own neutral state, and show missing turbine data as a separate state. B is equally well structured and links the grid to the alarms through matching IDs, but its idea of blocks growing when they escalate makes the layout less predictable. A's numbering skips 6, which is only cosmetic.
